_comment: Mutations that put the HOSTLESS-WebSocket-URL hole back.
The shared guard (bot_module/screener_feed.py) checks the scheme with a
PREFIX test -- 'ws://' or 'wss://'. That accepts 'ws://' and
'ws:///ws/main': a WebSocket URL that names NO HOST at all. There is
nothing to connect to, so the feed reconnects forever against an empty
address while the deployment keeps looking healthy.
The regime predicate (bot_module/regime_feed.py) had the same shape of
check, and it answers a DIFFERENT question -- 'can THIS deployment
deliver the regime data?' -- so a hostless URL made it answer YES: the
regime-change stop was armed against a feed that could never deliver.
Both mutations are watched by DB-FREE tests only, because the mutation
harness runs pytest under WSL ($HOME/dstest/bin/python) and that
interpreter cannot reach the Postgres test DB on localhost:5432 (measured
2026-11-03: ConnectionRefusedError). A whole-file target would ERROR on
every DB-backed test, and the harness counts an error as a kill -- a false
kill that would prove nothing about these mutants.
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: H1: the shared guard accepts a ws:// URL with NO HOST again
mutations.replace:
if False:  # MUTANT: a WebSocket URL with no host is accepted
        return _no_host_message(text)

mutations.label: H2: the regime predicate accepts a ws:// URL with NO HOST again
mutations.replace: return True  # MUTANT: the host is not required
